purpose: Prioritize mature draft/noindex Lab pages for human review using both structural readiness and claim-level factual-review coverage without automatically publishing or verifying a page.
scope: Human routes referenced by the SAP Lead assessment catalog and assessment authoring tools.

structural_checks.rule: title, description, permalink, last_modified_at, and tags are present
source body contains at least 1500 non-frontmatter characters
source contains at least two internal /labs/ links
source links to at least one /data/ or machine-readable assessment contract
source does not contain TODO, TBD, placeholder, lorem ipsum, or coming soon markers

evidence_checks: claim-level factual review is read from /labs/assessment/data/factual-review.json
source conflicts and unclear release scope are higher priority than normal unreviewed content
mature enterprise knowledge without factual review is prioritized before already source-supported routes
source-supported routes still require page-level human verification
verified:false never becomes verified through this audit

readiness_states.human_review_candidate: At least four structural checks pass and the page is still draft/noindex. Human review is the next action.
readiness_states.needs_structure: Fewer than four structural checks pass. Improve the page before factual promotion review.
readiness_states.public_or_indexable: The page is already outside the draft/noindex boundary. Audit only reports it; it does not change policy.
readiness_states.missing_source: The catalog points to a human route that cannot be resolved to a Lab source file.

promotion_rule: This audit never changes status, robots, sitemap, or verified frontmatter. Promotion requires an explicit human-reviewed repository change.
priority_rule: For human-review candidates, enterprise knowledge with source conflicts, unclear release scope, or no factual review is P0. Source-supported enterprise knowledge is P1. Assessment and authoring routes are P2 unless another policy explicitly raises them.
anti_shortcut_rules: Do not treat page length as factual quality.
Do not promote a page because CI is green.
Do not infer verified:true from the presence of source links.
Do not remove noindex from assessment or research pages merely to improve discoverability metrics.
Keep machine-readable data and human presentation aligned before promotion.
Do not treat source-supported claims as page-level verification.
